tower.presence.publishes: Approving it also publishes “{title}”: everybody in {country} is told {company} runs SeeBuyGet there from today, and asked to agree.
tower.docs.seeded: inserted with the system on {when}, not yet written by anybody here
tower.docs.ownProposal: You wrote this version, so a different person must publish it.
tower.docs.unchanged: {n, plural, one {… # line unchanged} other {… # lines unchanged}}
tower.docs.f.title: Title
tower.docs.f.bodyHint: A blank line between paragraphs. "## " starts a heading, "- " a list line, **two stars** make bold, [words](/privacy/) a link. Nothing else is read as anything but text.
tower.docs.f.notePlaceholder: Shown beside this version, to staff and on the public page
tower.docs.f.noteHint: People reading the page see this note, and everybody it concerns is told it in their app: write it for them.
tower.docs.f.askAgain: Everybody must agree to this version
tower.docs.f.askAgainHint: Tick it when the change asks something new of people, or takes something from them: everybody who agreed to an earlier version is asked again in their app before they go on. Leave it for clearer wording: the new version is shown, and nobody is asked.
tower.docs.nothingChanged: Nothing differs from the published version yet.
tower.docs.needsSecond: It changes nothing until a different person publishes it.
tower.trail.title: The trail
tower.trail.lede: Each step anchored in the chain as it was kept, and checked now against the record as it stands.
tower.staffReads.title: What staff opened
tower.staffReads.lede: Every record a member of staff opened by its name or number — a shop, a person, a parcel, a hold — with who, when, and how many times in a row. Lists are not in it. Looking here is in it too.
tower.staffReads.recordPlaceholder: A number, a code, an id
tower.conn.title: Connections
tower.conn.lede: What this server is connected to: a routing server and the adviser for the fleets’ planning, and email, push and the text that carries a code for everybody. All are set where the server runs. This says whether each is set up, whether it is answering, and whether what is written here leaves at all.
tower.conn.unread: This could not be read. Try again in a moment.
tower.conn.router.title: Routing server
tower.conn.router.off: No routing server is set, so every day’s plan is made on estimated distances: straight lines with an allowance for the road. Each plan says so to the office that made it.
tower.conn.router.invalid: What is set is not a web address, so no plan can use it. Every day’s plan is made on estimated distances, and tells its office the routing server could not be reached.
tower.conn.router.unasked: No plan has asked it since this server started ({since}). Check it now to see whether it answers.
tower.conn.router.answered: The last plan to ask, at {when}, was answered: road distances for its {n, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}.
tower.conn.router.failed: The last plan to ask, at {when}, got no road distances for its {n, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}: {why}. It was made on estimated distances, and said so.
tower.conn.router.where: Set on the server as GLOS_ROUTER_URL: the address of an OSRM-compatible routing server, your own or anybody’s that speaks it. GLOS_ROUTER_PROFILE and GLOS_ROUTER_MAX_POINTS are the other two. Only coordinates are sent to it — no order, no name, no address.
tower.conn.fact.notAnAddress: Set, and not a web address
tower.conn.fact.mostValue: {n} — a day with more is planned on estimates
tower.conn.fact.tableValue: {n, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}, every one to every other — measured {when}
tower.conn.fact.tableNone: Not measured yet: journeys, arrival times and bag pay use the estimate until they are
tower.conn.check.what: A check asks for the road distance between a fleet’s depot and a place a little way off it. Nothing is kept from it.
tower.conn.check.ok: It answered in {ms} ms: {km} km by road between two places {apart} km apart, near the depot of {near}.
tower.conn.check.odd: It answered in {ms} ms — with {km} km by road between two places that are {apart} km apart, near the depot of {near}. That cannot be the road between them: the server may hold another country’s map.
tower.conn.check.noRoad: It answered in {ms} ms, and knows no road between two places {apart} km apart near the depot of {near}. The server may hold another country’s map.
tower.conn.adviser.title: The adviser
tower.conn.adviser.off: No key is set, so a fleet’s office that asks the adviser is told it is not set up. Plans are made all the same: the adviser explains a plan and changes what is asked of it, and the plan itself never needed it.
tower.conn.adviser.unasked: No office has asked it since this server started ({since}). It is not checked from here: a question to it is a question paid for.
tower.conn.adviser.answered: The last office to ask, at {when}, was answered.
tower.conn.adviser.refused: The last office to ask, at {when}, was told the adviser is not set up: the key set on this server was refused. Check the key.
tower.conn.adviser.busy: The last office to ask, at {when}, was told it is busy: the service was limiting requests, or overloaded. That passes on its own, and a plan was given all the same.
tower.conn.adviser.unreachable: The last office to ask, at {when}, got no answer: the service could not be reached, or failed. A plan was given all the same.
tower.conn.adviser.where: Set on the server as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The key is never shown, here or anywhere.
tower.conn.mail.title: Email
tower.conn.mail.kept: No email leaves this server. Each one is written and kept here instead, and reaches nobody — {n} since it started. That is how a sandbox is meant to run.
tower.conn.mail.keptLive: No email leaves this server. Reset codes, invitations and notices are written and reach nobody — {n} since it started. This is not a sandbox: the people they were for are waiting. The provider’s token and its sending address have to be set before this server is relied on.
tower.conn.mail.tokenUnused: A provider’s token is set, and this server is not sending with it. It reads the token when it starts: restart it.
tower.conn.mail.problem.no_address: A token is set and the provider’s sending address is not, so nothing uses the token. Set ZEPTOMAIL_URL to the address your provider account shows on its API page, and restart the server.
tower.conn.mail.problem.not_an_address: A token is set, and what is set as the provider’s sending address is not a web address, so nothing is sent to it. Copy it again from your provider account’s API page, and restart the server.
tower.conn.mail.problem.not_https: A token is set, and the provider’s sending address is not an https address. The token would travel where anybody on the way could read it, so nothing is sent to it.
tower.conn.mail.noFrom: Email is sent as {from}. That is on a domain set aside for examples, which nobody owns, so no provider delivers for it. Set MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS to an address on a domain your provider has verified.
tower.conn.mail.unsent: No email has been written since this server started ({since}).
tower.conn.mail.sent: The last email, at {when}, was handed to the provider: “{what}”. Whether it arrived is the provider’s to say.
tower.conn.mail.failed.unreachable: The last email, at {when}, could not be handed over: the provider could not be reached, or did not answer in time. It was “{what}”.
tower.conn.mail.failed.failed: The last email, at {when}, could not be handed over: what came back from the provider’s address was a fault, or was not the provider’s answer at all. It was “{what}”.
tower.conn.mail.failed.rejected: The last email, at {when}, was turned down by the provider. It was “{what}”. That is one email: others may be going.
tower.conn.mail.failed.limit: The last email, at {when}, was not taken: the provider’s sending limit or credit is used up, and nothing is delivered until that is put right. It was “{what}”.
tower.conn.mail.failed.refused: The last email, at {when}, was refused by the provider, and nothing is delivered until that is put right. It was “{what}”.
tower.conn.mail.refusedWhy.token: It did not accept the token.
tower.conn.mail.refusedWhy.sender: The address email is sent as is on a domain the provider has not verified for this account.
tower.conn.mail.refusedWhy.review: The provider has not approved the account for sending yet.
tower.conn.mail.refusedWhy.blocked: The provider has blocked the account.
tower.conn.mail.refusedWhy.unknown: It will not send for this account as it is set up. Check the token, that the sending address is the one your account shows, and that email is sent as an address on a domain the provider has verified.
tower.conn.mail.lastKept: That email is kept, and will be tried again.
tower.conn.mail.lastLost: That email will not be sent again, and the person it was for was not told.
tower.conn.mail.waiting: Waiting to be tried again: {n}, the oldest since {since}. They wait in this server’s memory: restarting it loses them.
tower.conn.mail.sentLater: Handed over on a later try since it started: {n}.
tower.conn.mail.bounces.deaf: Nothing listens for email that comes back, so an address that bounces goes on being written to.
tower.conn.mail.bounces.refused: Signed bounce notices are being refused: {n} since it started, the last at {when}, and none has been taken since.
tower.conn.mail.bounces.why.mismatch: Its signature is not this server’s key’s: compare ZEPTOMAIL_WEBHOOK_KEY with the authentication key on the provider’s webhook.
tower.conn.mail.bounces.why.unsigned: It carried no signature this server can read.
tower.conn.mail.bounces.why.algorithm: It was signed in a way this server does not know.
tower.conn.mail.bounces.why.stale: Its time was not now: check this server’s clock.
tower.conn.mail.bounces.why.unreadable: It was signed with the key, and is not a notice this server can read.
tower.conn.mail.bounces.why.not_raw: This server is not reading that address as the bytes it arrives in, so no signature can be checked. That is in how the server is started, not in the provider.
tower.conn.mail.whereBounces: To hear of email that comes back, add a webhook at the provider for hard and soft bounces, pointed at /v1/mail/provider/events on this server’s public address, and set the webhook’s authentication key here as ZEPTOMAIL_WEBHOOK_KEY. An address email came back from for good is not written to again until its owner confirms it with a code; a code is always sent. A request with no signature is counted and nothing more: the address is public, and something will always find it — but if the provider’s own show up there, its webhook has no authentication key. No notice has yet come from the real provider: the first one should be watched here.
tower.conn.mail.gaveUp: Given up on since it started: {n} — turned down, possibly already sent, or no longer worth sending.
tower.conn.mail.someFailed: Since this server started, {failed} of {n} could not be handed over at the first try.
tower.conn.mail.where: Email is sent through ZeptoMail (Zoho CPaaS) when the server is started with both ZEPTOMAIL_TOKEN and ZEPTOMAIL_URL: the token and the sending address, each as your provider account shows it on its API page. The token is never shown, here or anywhere, and the address is shown as its host only. The address email is sent as is MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS. A notice that could not be handed over is tried again — after a minute, then five, fifteen, and every hour, for one to three days — while it waits in this server’s memory; a code is never sent late. An email to an address that cannot exist (example.com, or one ending .example or .test) is not handed to the provider: it could only bounce.
tower.conn.mail.whereKept: On a sandbox, what was kept can be read at /v1/mail/outbox on this server, and every email looked at with sample words at /v1/mail/preview.
tower.conn.push.title: Push to a phone
tower.conn.push.kept: No push leaves this server. A notification is always written to the person’s bell in their app; the push that would light a phone whose app is closed is kept here instead. That is how a sandbox is meant to run.
tower.conn.push.keptLive: No push leaves this server. A notification is written to the person’s bell and waits there until they open their app; no phone is woken. This is not a sandbox: a driver handed a trip finds out when they next look. A push sender has to be put in before this server is relied on.
tower.conn.push.mismatched: The two keys this server signs with do not belong together: one was set and the other left as it was, or they were copied from two different pairs. A phone enrols against one and the server signs with the other, so every push is refused. Set both, from the same pair.
tower.conn.push.builtIn: This server signs with the key written in its own source code, and anybody who can read the code can sign with it too. Give it a key of its own (GLOS_VAPID_PRIVATE) before this server is relied on.
tower.conn.push.unsent: No push has been handed to a phone since this server started ({since}).
tower.conn.push.sent: The last push, at {when}, was handed to the phone’s push service.
tower.conn.push.failed: The last push, at {when}, could not be handed over. The notification is in the person’s bell all the same.
tower.conn.push.someFailed: Since this server started, {failed} of {n} could not be handed over.
tower.conn.push.where: The keys are set on the server as GLOS_VAPID_PUBLIC and GLOS_VAPID_PRIVATE; the private one is never shown, here or anywhere. Changing them ends every enrolment: each phone has to turn notifications on again.
tower.conn.sms.ownerCodes: Stand-in codes are on until the end of {until} (UTC): {numbers, plural, one {# number} other {# numbers}} and {addresses, plural, one {# address} other {# addresses}} set in GLOS_STANDIN_CODES on the server take the codes set there, as if texted or mailed — nothing is sent, nothing shown. They stop when texts (or mail) leave, or on that day.
tower.conn.sms.title: Text messages
tower.conn.sms.kept: No text leaves this server. A code is handed back to the app that asked for it and shown on its screen; the text that would have carried it is kept here — {n} since it started. That is how a sandbox is meant to run.
tower.conn.sms.reviewLive: No text leaves this server, and the review code is on until the end of {until} (UTC): a NEW account’s number — and the recovery email a PIN asks for — is confirmed with 000000, shown on the screen. It never signs in to an account that exists: a new phone or browser, a new PIN or a payout number still wait for a real text. Not for real people: set Twilio, and remove GLOS_REVIEW_CODE_UNTIL.
tower.conn.sms.keptLive: No text leaves this server, and this is not a sandbox: a code has no other way to a phone. Nobody can sign up, confirm a new phone or browser, or replace a PIN — each is told the code could not be sent. Twilio’s account, a credential and what texts are sent from have to be set before this server is relied on.
tower.conn.sms.problem.no_account: Something of Twilio’s is set and the account is not. Set TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, and restart the server.
tower.conn.sms.problem.no_credential: Twilio’s account is set and there is nothing to sign with. Set TWILIO_API_KEY_SID with TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET, or TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, and restart the server.
tower.conn.sms.problem.no_sender: Twilio’s account is set and nothing says who a text is from. Set TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID, or TWILIO_FROM, and restart the server.
tower.conn.sms.problem.not_twilio: TWILIO_URL is set. It is only for a stand-in on the same machine as a sandbox; anywhere else the credential would go to an address that is not Twilio’s, so nothing is sent. Remove it, and restart the server.
tower.conn.sms.problem.sandbox: Twilio’s account is set, and this is a sandbox, which does not text: its people are made up, and a made-up number may be somebody’s.
tower.conn.sms.standIn: Texts go to a stand-in on this machine, not to Twilio: no phone receives one.
tower.conn.sms.unsent: No code has been texted since this server started ({since}).
tower.conn.sms.sent: The last code, at {when}, was handed to Twilio. Whether it reached the phone is Twilio’s to say: this server does not hear of it.
tower.conn.sms.sentStandIn: The last code, at {when}, was taken by it.
tower.conn.sms.failed.unreachable: The last code, at {when}, could not be texted: Twilio could not be reached, or did not answer in time. The person was told it could not be sent, and can ask again at once.
tower.conn.sms.failed.failed: The last code, at {when}, could not be texted: what came back was a fault, or was not Twilio’s answer at all. The person was told it could not be sent, and can ask again at once.
tower.conn.sms.failed.limit: The last code, at {when}, was not taken: Twilio asked this server to slow down. The person was told it could not be sent, and can ask again at once.
tower.conn.sms.failed.rejected: The last code, at {when}, could not be texted to the number it was for: Twilio cannot text that number. The person was told to check it. That is one number: others may be going.
tower.conn.sms.failed.refused: The last code, at {when}, was refused by Twilio, and the person was told it could not be sent.
tower.conn.sms.refusedWhy.credential: It did not accept the credential, or the credential may not send. Nobody is texted until that is put right.
tower.conn.sms.refusedWhy.country: The country that number is in is not switched on in the Twilio account’s SMS Geo Permissions. Numbers in other countries may be going.
tower.conn.sms.refusedWhy.sender: What texts are sent from is not something this Twilio account can send messages with. Nobody is texted until that is put right.
tower.conn.sms.refusedWhy.trial: The Twilio account texts only numbers that were verified with it, until it is upgraded.
tower.conn.sms.refusedWhy.unknown: It will not text for this account as it is set up. Check the credential, and what texts are sent from.
tower.conn.sms.pausedHour: Texting is paused since {since}: {n} codes in the last hour reached the cap of {cap}, and {held, plural, one {# code was} other {# codes were}} not sent. It resumes by itself as the hour moves on. If this is real growth, raise GLOS_SMS_PER_HOUR on the server; if it is not, somebody may be asking for codes to run up the bill.
tower.conn.sms.pausedDay: Texting is paused since {since}: {n} codes in the last day reached the cap of {cap}, and {held, plural, one {# code was} other {# codes were}} not sent. It resumes by itself as the day moves on. If this is real growth, raise GLOS_SMS_PER_DAY on the server; if it is not, somebody may be asking for codes to run up the bill.
tower.conn.sms.failed.paused: The last code, at {when}, was not sent: texting was paused at its cap. The person was told codes are paused for a while.
tower.conn.fact.smsCapValue: {hour} of {perHour} in the last hour · {day} of {perDay} in the last day
tower.conn.sms.someFailed: Since this server started, {failed} of {n} could not be handed over.
tower.conn.sms.where: A code is texted through Twilio when the server is started, off a sandbox, with TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, a credential (TWILIO_API_KEY_SID with TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET, or TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN) and what texts are sent from (TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID, or TWILIO_FROM). None of them is shown, here or anywhere. A code is texted only to a number in a country that is switched on (Where we operate): there is no list beside it. Twilio keeps a list of its own, changed by hand in its console and not by us: switch on the same countries, and no others, under its SMS Geo Permissions. A text is sent once: when it cannot be handed over, the person is told, and asks again. No text has yet gone through the real provider: the first one should be watched here.
tower.conn.sms.whereKept: On a sandbox no phone is needed: the code is shown on the screen that asked for it.
tower.conn.fact.smsCountries: Countries a code is texted to
tower.conn.fact.smsCountriesNone: None — no country is switched on
tower.conn.fact.smsFenced: Not texted: the number’s country is not switched on
tower.conn.fact.reserved: Left unsent: addresses that cannot exist
tower.conn.fact.bouncesDeaf: Not listened for — no key is set
tower.conn.fact.bouncesNone: Listened for — none has come since it started
tower.conn.fact.bouncesSome: Listened for — {received} taken, {refused} signed and refused, {unsigned} with no signature
tower.conn.fact.stopped: Addresses not written to: email came back
tower.conn.fact.bounced: Left unsent: email to the address came back
tower.conn.fact.sentLater: Handed over on a later try
tower.conn.fact.countFailedFirst: {n} — {failed} could not be handed over at the first try
tower.conn.fact.keys.built_in: The pair written in the source code
tower.conn.fact.keys.mismatched: Two that do not belong together
tower.conn.since: What each last met is kept since this server started, {since}. A restart forgets it.
tower.presence.title: Where we operate
tower.presence.lede: What the network is allowed to do in each country. Matching, custody and proof work everywhere; charging, holding money and answering for goods need a company on the ground.
tower.presence.caveatT: A standing is a permission, never a launch announcement.
tower.presence.caveat: A country low on this list still moves goods and still proves it. What it cannot do is charge anybody, hold anybody’s money, or promise cover nothing can pay — and where we cannot pay a claim, the cover is zero rather than unstated.
tower.presence.derived: has a company — nothing decided by hand
tower.presence.f.termsHint: Two sets, because the terms are not symmetric about a border. Everything is off until you tick it, and switching one on needs a second person.
tower.presence.f.termsCare: The two marked ! are the ones that usually go wrong: EXW makes a foreign buyer file the export, DDP makes a foreign seller the importer of record. Prefer FCA and DAP unless somebody has checked.
tower.presence.needsCompany: No company of ours is ready here yet. Established is what a registered company MEANS — create it under The companies, complete its record and have its papers verified, then propose it here.
tower.presence.needsPartner: No partner company is ready here yet. Record the local partner under The companies, complete its record and have its papers verified, then propose it here.
tower.presence.sameCapabilities: Nothing this country may do would change.
tower.presence.noChange: Pick a different standing to see what it would change.
tower.presence.needCode: Which country? Choose it from the list.
tower.presence.badCode: That is not a country in the catalogue.
tower.presence.comingHint: Shops, hubs, stores, fleets and couriers can sign up here and have their papers checked. Nothing moves until the country is opened. Whoever asked to be told hears that they can sign up now, and again on the day it opens.
tower.presence.comingAfterOpen: This country has opened already. Taking sign-ups is for a country that has not: to stop new work here, choose Observed.
tower.presence.needsRate: The rate book has no exchange rate for this country’s money yet. Put one on the rate book first — the network cannot switch on a country it cannot price in.
tower.presence.needsSecond: This gives the country something it cannot do now, so a second person must approve it.
tower.presence.testersOnlyHint: Only the numbers on the test list sign up, sign in and are sent codes. Everybody else is told it opens soon, and can leave an email. Shops and hubs here stay off the public map.
